The smoke in the dream clears, and I look upon the shape that speaks of Wewush. 

We have grain enough in our jars, more than these walls shall need before the autumn brings its yield again. If they have empty bellies and cry out in the cold, it is a hard thing to let kin or neighbour starve while our own granary groans. 

Tell me, spirit—are these people of Wewush truly hungry, or do they seek to dull their axes and sharpen their spears against our gates once their bellies are full? If they come in peace, we might spare a measure of wheat. What do you truly see when you look upon their hearths?

Our bins of grain are full to bursting, but a house cannot burn wheat to keep the frost from the little ones, nor can we chew dry stalks forever. Tell me truly, does your rain bring more than wet mud, or is this just another trick of the clouds?
I know the wind well enough; it cools our skin in the heat and strips the thatch if we tie it poorly. If you are that wind, you have no need of sleeping minds. Speak plainly, or let the night pass.
